title: 2017 AMC 12A Problem 15
statement: Let \(f(x)=\sin x+2\cos x+3\tan x,\) using radian measure for the variable \(x.\) In what interval does the smallest positive value of \(x\) for which \(f(x)=0\) lie?

solutions.text:
For \(0\lt x\lt\dfrac{\pi}{2}\) all three terms are positive, so \(f(x)\gt0.\) For \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\lt x\lt\pi,\) set \(s=\sin x\gt0\) and \(t=-\cos x\gt0.\) Since \(0\lt t\le1,\) \[ \begin{aligned} f(x)&=s-2t-\dfrac{3s}{t} \\ &=-2t-s\left(\dfrac{3}{t}-1\right)\lt0. \end{aligned} \] Thus no root occurs before \(x=\pi.\)

At \(x=\pi,\) \(f(\pi)=0+2(-1)+0=-2\lt0.\) At \(x=\dfrac{5\pi}{4},\) \(\tan x=1\) so \(f=-\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}+3\gt0.\) By the intermediate value theorem the smallest positive root lies in \(\left(\pi,\dfrac{5\pi}{4}\right).\)

Since \(\pi\gt3\) and \(\dfrac{5\pi}{4}\lt4,\) this interval sits inside \((3,4).\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: For \(0\lt x\lt\dfrac{\pi}{2}\) all three terms are positive, so there is no root there
Just past \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\) the term \(3\tan x\) makes \(f\) negative; locate the first sign change after \(\pi\)
